{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793058536358,"sessionID":"ses_e85628b6dffe8DQ2bTx065rB2R","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"edit","callID":"toolu_015uBZY9bE122xhPUZwPN2MR","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/floydwarshall_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r4/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp","oldString":"void floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm\n    // For each intermediate node k\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n        // For each source node i\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n            // For each destination node j\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < numNodes; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distIK = dist[idx2(k, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distKJ = dist[idx2(j, k, numNodes)];\n                \n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + distKJ;\n                \n                if (newDist < distIJ) {\n                    dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = newDist;\n                    path[idx2(j, i, numNodes)] = k;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}","newString":"void floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm, parallelized with OpenMP.\n    //\n    // Within phase k, row i of the matrix is updated using only row i itself\n    // and row k. Row k is never modified during phase k (its diagonal entry is\n    // zero, so relaxing through k cannot improve it), and the diagonal entry is\n    // zero for the whole run. Therefore rows are independent within a phase and\n    // the result is identical to the sequential order of updates.\n    //\n    // Storage: idx2(j, i, n) = i * n + j, so row i is contiguous in memory.\n    // A single parallel region is opened for the whole computation; the\n    // implicit barrier at the end of each \"omp for\" enforces the dependency\n    // between consecutive phases k.\n    const size_t n = numNodes;\n    unsigned int* const d = dist.data();\n    unsigned int* const p = path.data();\n\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n            const unsigned int* const rowK = d + k * n;\n\n            #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n            for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n                // Row k is unchanged in phase k (see above), so skip it.\n                if (i == k) {\n                    continue;\n                }\n\n                unsigned int* const rowI = d + i * n;\n                unsigned int* const pathI = p + i * n;\n\n                // dist[i][k] is not changed in phase k (relaxing it would add\n                // dist[k][k] == 0), so it can be hoisted out of the j loop.\n                const unsigned int distIK = rowI[k];\n\n                for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n                    const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n                    if (newDist < rowI[j]) {\n                        rowI[j] = newDist;\n                        pathI[j] = static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}"},"output":"Edit applied successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"diff":"Index: /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/floydwarshall_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r4/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp\n===================================================================\n--- /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/floydwarshall_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r4/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp\n+++ /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/floydwarshall_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r4/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp\n@@ -43,25 +43,50 @@\n \n void floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist, \n                    std::vector<unsigned int>& path, \n                    const size_t numNodes) {\n-    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm\n-    // For each intermediate node k\n-    for (size_t k = 0; {"type":"text","timestamp":1793058574606,"sessionID":"ses_e85628b6dffe8DQ2bTx065rB2R","part":{"id":"prt_17a9e86440012UWfA96hXuxuHy","messageID":"msg_17a9e8125001KFVKbi7amyzvig","sessionID":"ses_e85628b6dffe8DQ2bTx065rB2R","type":"text","text":"The Floyd-Warshall kernel is now parallelized with OpenMP, and OpenMP is a hard requirement in CMake. Output matches the original exactly, and at n=2048 it runs about 4.4x faster on one thread and about 90x faster on 32 threads.\n\n**Changes (only the two existing files):**\n\n- **`floydwarshall.cpp`**: `floydWarshall()` opens one parallel region for the whole computation. Each phase `k` runs `omp for schedule(static)` over rows `i`. Rows are independent within a phase, since row `k` is never modified during phase `k` (the diagonal is zero). The implicit barrier at the end of each `omp for` keeps phases ordered. The inner loop uses row pointers and hoists `dist[i][k]`, which removes the index math from the hot loop.\n- **`CMakeLists.txt`**: added `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and linked `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. The existing `-O3 -march=native` flags and the `m` link are kept. The executable name is unchanged.\n\n**Verification:**\n\n- The original project includes `../common/results_output.hpp`, which doesn't exist in this workspace, so the original can't build as-is. I tested with a stub header placed outside the project.\n- Distance-matrix hashes and validation results match the original for n = 1, 2, 7, 100, 300, 513, and 1000 at 1, 4, 16, and 64 threads.\n- The build has no warnings under `-Wall -Wextra`.\n- The path matrix isn't printed, so I checked it only by reasoning, not by output comparison.\n\n**Timing (n=2048, `-n 2048`):**\n\n| Threads | Time (ms) | GOPS |\n|---|---|---|\n| original | 9393 | — |\n| 1 | 2140 | 4.0 |\n| 4 | 562 | 15.3 |\n| 16 | 173 | 49.7 |\n| 32 | 103 | 83.4 |\n\nThe matrix initialization is still serial. It is O(n²) and uses a seeded `rand_r` sequence, so changing it would change the generated graph. It is not included in the timed region.","time":{"start":1793058571844,"end":1793058574602}}}
